title: Isolated Downstream Validation and Single-Repair Effects in Intent-to-Configuration NetOps: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study cand-003-stud-001) that isolates purely downstream deterministic validation plus a bounded single-repair intervention under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using 1,000 deterministic intents drawn from a synthetic workflow stress corpus and a deterministic digital-twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; therefore any paired outcome difference can arise only from the deterministic validator decision and at most one permitted repair call (guarded arm). Observed outcomes: baseline safe-deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe-deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; discordants n10 = 5 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only). The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.001, 0.01] and is reported as a descriptive summary. Total hosted model calls recorded = 1,005 (1,000 shared initial + 5 repair). We present the exact McNemar as the preregistered confirmatory inference and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit (0.005) in light of sparse discordant counts, ceiling effects, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating translation from operator intent to device configuration can improve operational throughput but creates safety risks: incorrect command ordering, transient invariant violations, and touches of protected fields may convert plausible high-level plans into damaging live changes. Large-language-model (LLM) planners and sequence generators show well-documented sensitivity to prompts and decoding settings and a non-negligible rate of syntactic and semantic errors in structured outputs [https://openalex.org/W4414677042, https://openalex.org/W4411523078]. These findings motivate verifier-augmented architectures (generate→validate→repair) and digital-twin emulators as governance and safety elements in NetOps pipelines [https://openalex.org/W7163777690, https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18233].

Despite this motivation, many prior evaluations conflate downstream verifier effects with independent changes in generation (different prompts or decoding), complicating causal attribution. This paper reports a preregistered paired experiment explicitly designed to isolate only the downstream deterministic validator decision plus a single bounded repair (generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate). Under these semantics the same initial sampled candidate is reused for baseline and guarded conditions, so the estimand is precisely the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) attributable to deterministic validation and at most one validator-triggered repair. Our objective is narrow and causal: quantify the marginal downstream safety return of a deterministic digital-twin validator and a single permitted repair when generator output is fixed.
sections.related_work:
Empirical work on structured generation documents that LLM outputs are sensitive to prompt and decoding choices and that hallucinations and structural errors frequently affect downstream executability and correctness [https://openalex.org/W4414677042, https://openalex.org/W4411523078]. Two complementary technical responses have received attention: (1) constraint-aware or schema-constrained decoding approaches that enforce structural correctness at generation time, and (2) post-generation verification and repair using formal, rule-based, or emulator-based validators. Method-development papers in constrained decoding report improved executable output rates in structured domains (for example, cheminformatics), but those results are domain-dependent and rely on the tooling that enforces constraints [10.26434/chemrxiv.15005091/v1].

Separate system and benchmark papers evaluate generate→validate→repair architectures and digital-twin validators in NetOps or related settings. Several of these works report that verifier-augmented pipelines can reduce observable errors under controlled scenarios, while also noting that measured improvement magnitude depends on validator coverage, the benchmark's failure modes, and the evaluation design [https://openalex.org/W7163777690, https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18233]. Importantly, those reported gains are heterogeneous and often arise in studies where generation conditions differ between arms; such designs confound generator improvements with downstream adjudication effects. The literature therefore motivates isolating downstream marginal returns by holding generation constant, a rationale we implement here via shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Agentic NetOps and governance-focused proposals emphasize protocol-mediated execution, auditability, and bounded tool interfaces (canaries, rollbacks, proof-carrying traces) as complements to any single model's behavior [10.2139/ssrn.6426760, https://openalex.org/W7161165783]. These architectural perspectives frame validators and repair as necessary but not sufficient components: validator fidelity and orchestration policy determine operational reliability. Our study complements these lines by measuring the downstream, marginal effect of a deterministic validator plus one permitted repair when the generator output is fixed.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and experimental design. The study is preregistered as cand-003-stud-001. The confirmatory design is paired binary with task_count = 1,000 complete pairs, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1, independent_condition_generation = false, and the primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The primary confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar; a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) was prespecified as a descriptive summary. These choices were frozen before any hosted-model calls and are documented in the preregistration.

Task corpus, selection rule, and topology patterns. Tasks derive deterministically from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus. The deterministic selection rule yields exactly 1,000 unique intents spanning multi-step workflows that exercise ordering constraints, transient invariants, and protected-field prohibitions. Tasks carry annotated difficulty levels ('very_hard' and 'extreme') and pattern labels (for example, safe_access_service_transfer, failover_then_offline_reconfiguration, rolling_access_vlan_migration, composed_redundancy_and_access_maintenance) that indicate the types of dependency constraints the validator checks.

Adapter, model configuration, and validator semantics. The adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the declared provider/model was gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses). The recorded model configuration logs temperature = null/unset; null/unset is explicitly not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling (it does not imply temperature = 0). Exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms (shared_initial_candidate): baseline outcome equals the initial single-shot validity of that candidate; guarded outcome equals final validity after deterministic validation and any permitted single repair. The validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 is a rule-based digital twin that parses candidate command sequences, checks required command presence/order, protected-field noninterference, and workflow invariants; it emits a binary safe-deploy decision and structured traces (validation_before, repair_applied, validation_after). Guarded episodes may invoke at most one repair call and, when invoked, the repair call is the sole source of paired outcome differences under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics.

Causal interpretation and internal controls. Because the pair reuses the same initial candidate, any discordant outcome can only result from (a) the deterministic validator rejecting or accepting the shared candidate differently when applied as part of the guarded pipeline versus the baseline adjudication semantics, or (b) a validator-triggered repair that produces an accepted replacement. No independent first-pass generations, prompt modifications, or decoding changes were executed for this run; planned independent-generation arms in the preregistration were not executed and therefore do not enter this analysis. This design isolates downstream validator/repair marginal effects but precludes measuring generation-time interventions.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. Planned episodes = 2,000; completed = 2,000; complete_pairs = 1,000; failed episodes = 0. Provider-call auditing recorded hosted model call event count = 1,005 consisting of 1,000 shared initial generations and 5 repair invocations; no hosted-model calls failed and there were no cache hits. The analysis executor computed all confirmatory statistics using the recorded paired outcomes and the preregistered seeds.

Primary paired outcomes (preregistered). The observed paired contingency table is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625, which does not meet the preregistered two-sided α = 0.05.

Paired bootstrap descriptive summary. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) produced by the registered executor is [0.001, 0.01]. This descriptive interval excludes zero in this run despite the confirmatory p-value exceeding 0.05; this pattern arises from the discreteness of the paired null distribution when total discordants (n10 + n01) are extremely small.

Repair diagnostics and failure modes. Exactly five validator-triggered repairs occurred and correspond to the five guarded-only successes (n10 = 5). Archived validator traces for those repaired pairs document that the shared initial candidate was rejected for rule-level violations—principally required-sequence ordering violations and unauthorized touches of protected interfaces—and that a single repair call produced an alternative candidate which the validator accepted on revalidation. The repaired episodes are concentrated among higher-difficulty patterns annotated 'very_hard' or 'extreme' and involve multi-step required sequences; with only five repaired cases we cannot robustly estimate per-pattern repair efficacy, but the qualitative failure-mode pattern is consistent with dependency-induced ordering vulnerabilities in complex workflows.

Compact accounting summary. Planned episodes = 2,000; completed = 2,000; complete pairs = 1,000; model calls used = 1,005; repair calls invoked = 5; baseline successes = 995; guarded successes = 1,000; paired difference = 0.005; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.0625; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.001, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729).
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory versus descriptive inference and discrete-test nuance. The preregistered confirmatory decision is the exact two-sided McNemar (p = 0.0625); under the preregistered two-sided α = 0.05 the study does not claim confirmatory support for a nonzero paired increase. The preregistered bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) is a registered descriptive summary produced by the executor and reported to aid interpretation; it does not override the preregistered confirmatory conclusion. When discordant counts are sparse (here total discordants = 5), the null distribution of exact paired tests is concentrated on a small set of outcomes and two-sided exact p-values can remain above conventional cutoffs while resampling-based percentile intervals exclude zero. This is a sampling-distribution phenomenon reflecting discreteness, not a contradiction in the recorded counts.

Power, ceiling effects, and sensitivity to operating point. The preregistered power calculation assumed baseline≈0.60 and targeted an absolute increase of 0.15 with task_count = 1,000 yielding >80% power for the paired McNemar-style test. Observed baseline = 0.995 departs substantially from that assumption and concentrates mass in the concordant success cell (n11 = 995), leaving only five discordant pairs for inference. Detecting the observed tiny absolute difference (0.005) at such a high baseline requires either dramatically larger paired sample sizes or design choices that increase discordant prevalence (for example, independent generation arms, injected failure cases, or a larger allowed repair budget). Therefore the null confirmatory result must be interpreted in the context of a mismatch between prespecified operating assumptions and the sampled operating point.

Failure-mode implications and diagnostic utility. Archived validator traces show repaired cases share rule-level failure modes: ordering violations in required_sequence and unauthorized touches of protected interfaces. These are precisely classes of errors that a rule-based digital-twin validator is designed to catch and, in our run, a single repair call often sufficed to produce an accepted corrected candidate. Although the absolute number of repairs (n = 5) is small, the qualitative pattern supports the operational hypothesis that validators focusing on ordering and protected-field constraints can avert concrete unsafe deployments in complex multi-step workflows. Quantifying average repair success, repair effectiveness by pattern, or cost–benefit tradeoffs across repair budgets requires a larger number of failures or different sampling/design choices.

Design tradeoffs and construct scope. The shared_initial_candidate paired design intentionally isolates downstream validator/repair marginal effects and avoids conflating validator outcomes with generator sampling or prompt engineering. This yields a precise causal estimand (baseline initial validity versus final guarded validity after deterministic validation and up to one repair) but precludes evaluation of generator interventions. Construct validity depends on validator coverage: omitted semantic checks would undercount failures and inflate apparent success. External validity is further limited by the synthetic corpus and single declared model (gpt-5-mini) used in this execution.

Operational implications and next steps. Artifact-grounded evidence indicates that deterministic validator + bounded single repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in structured NetOps tasks, but measurable marginal gains are small when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the repair budget is constrained. Supported, concrete follow-ups (all preregistered or documented in the archived manifest) include executing independent first-pass generation arms to measure generator+validator interactions, sweeping repair budgets (k > 1) to quantify marginal returns per repair, expanding validator rule suites and injecting targeted failure cases to increase discordant prevalence for sensitivity, and evaluating multiple model families and prompt/configuration variants. Each follow-up should prespecify baseline failure ranges and adjust power calculations to the expected operating regime.

Limitations revisited. Sparse discordant counts (n10 + n01 = 5), extreme baseline success, and validator scope jointly limit inferential resolution and external generalizability. The study was designed to answer a narrowly specified causal question and does so: the recorded paired difference arises solely from deterministic validation and at most one repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. However, the design cannot address whether alternative generation strategies, constrained decoding, or larger repair budgets would yield larger marginal improvements; those are distinct estimands that require independent execution arms.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1,000-task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single-shot generator; the preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test did not meet two-sided α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total hosted model calls recorded = 1,005. The preregistered confirmatory conclusion is the exact McNemar outcome; the paired bootstrap CI is a preregistered descriptive summary that aids interpretation. Artifact-grounded evidence indicates that deterministic downstream validation with a bounded single repair can prevent some unsafe outcomes in complex NetOps workflows, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design isolates downstream effects. Mapping operationally relevant marginal returns requires follow-ups that vary generator semantics, repair budgets, validator coverage, and model families.

Orchestration and validator: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the validator/digital twin. Preregistration: study cand-003-stud-001 (frozen prior to any model calls and recorded in the archived execution manifest). Immutable initial master prompt reference archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset (null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Human role and autonomy boundary: after the autonomy lock the research run executed the preregistered experiment, analysis, and manuscript drafting; no human manually edited the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Single-model scope: only the declared model gpt-5-mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first-pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two-sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one-sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post-hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe-deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi-device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
